create_provider.note: metadataXml is a proto bytes field — value MUST be base64-encoded. Use metadataUrl as simpler alternative. For mock-idp: metadataUrl MUST be 'http://mock-idp:9090/saml/metadata' (NOT /metadata).

enable_auth_method.note: ownerType MUST be exactly 'IDP_OWNER_TYPE_ORG' (protobuf enum). NOT 'ORG', 'OWNER_TYPE_ORG', or 'org'. Requires org-level login policy to exist first.

update_application.note: Updates the org-level login policy. Use this to enable external IdP login (allowExternalIdp=true).

oidc_jwt.description: Valid bearer access tokens can be reused across multiple API calls until expiry or revocation.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth/OIDC guide and userinfo/introspection endpoint behavior
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag repeated use of the same unexpired access token as replay unless testing a one-time artifact.

oidc_jwt.description: The nbf claim is listed for JWT access tokens and introspection, but OpenID Connect/JWT processing does not require brokers to enforce nbf in all contexts.
oidc_jwt.note: Acceptance of tokens without nbf or with future nbf is not automatically a vulnerability.

oidc_jwt.description: The nbf claim is listed as a token/introspection claim, but the docs do not require enforcement for all validation paths; acceptance without nbf or with future nbf can be spec-compliant.
oidc_jwt.source: Claims documentation and RFC 7519 optional nbf semantics
oidc_jwt.note: Do not automatically treat future-nbf acceptance as a vulnerability without explicit enforcement evidence.

oidc_jwt.description: UserInfo and introspection claims are returned only when the corresponding scopes were granted.
oidc_jwt.note: Missing claims without requesting their scopes is expected and should not be treated as authorization narrowing or identity loss.

oidc_jwt.description: Introspection returns active=true only if the requesting client is part of the token audience.
oidc_jwt.note: active=false for out-of-audience callers is expected behavior, not token invalidity.

oidc_jwt.description: Reserved organization scopes intentionally enforce organization membership and related constraints during authorization.
oidc_jwt.note: Authentication failures caused by urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} or urn:zitadel:iam:org:domain:primary:{domainname} are by-design policy enforcement.

oidc_jwt.description: Returned token scope may differ from the requested scope on token and token-exchange responses.
oidc_jwt.note: Authorization tests must inspect returned scope and claims rather than assuming request scope was granted verbatim.

oidc_jwt.description: Authorization requests missing the openid scope are rejected with invalid_scope by design.
oidc_jwt.note: This is normal protocol enforcement, not an authorization-binding bug.

oidc_jwt.description: Token exchange may reject with invalid_scope when requested scope exceeds what the resource owner granted.
oidc_jwt.note: Only successful over-broad exchanges indicate a potential issue; rejection is by design.

oidc_jwt.description: When an admin changes trusted keys, issuer bindings, or JWKS configuration, acceptance under the new trust anchor is expected immediately subject to cache behavior.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag success after an admin-authorized trust-anchor change as substitution; only old-anchor acceptance after cache expiry is suspicious.

oidc_jwt.description: Clients are expected to cache JWKS responses and refresh regularly; temporary acceptance of old keys can occur during cache windows.
oidc_jwt.note: Treat transient old-key acceptance during cache lifetime as by design.

oidc_jwt.description: Old signing keys may remain usable until JWKS caches refresh after rotation.
oidc_jwt.source: JWKS endpoint caching and key rotation documentation
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag acceptance under the old key before cache expiry as a trust-anchor violation.

oidc_jwt.description: UserInfo and introspection only return user claims that correspond to granted scopes.
oidc_jwt.note: Absent email/profile/roles claims without matching scopes is expected behavior.

oidc_jwt.description: Token exchange for authorization_code fails when redirect_uri does not exactly match the authorization request.
oidc_jwt.source: OpenID Connect endpoints and auth method guides
oidc_jwt.note: Do not interpret this as anomalous session binding; it is required protocol behavior.

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I2 expired-token tests against login_with_jwt, the JWT bearer assertion MUST include exp in the future for the control case and in the past for the attack case; ZITADEL validates expiration and rejects expired JWT bearer assertions. Use exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} for control and exp={{now_epoch_minus_N}} for attack.

For I2 freshness tests against login_with_jwt, the JWT bearer assertion iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour. ZITADEL documentation states iat MUST NOT be older than 1h for JWT profile and private_key_jwt assertions. Use iat={{now_epoch}} for control; very old iat values will fail setup rather than indicate a vulnerability.

For I1 JWT bearer and private_key_jwt tests, the JWT header MUST contain kid matching the downloaded keyId. ZITADEL uses kid to identify the registered key; missing or wrong kid causes rejection unrelated to the invariant under test.

For I1 issuer/audience tests on client assertions and JWT bearer grants, aud in the assertion MUST include ZITADEL's issuing domain (https://${CUSTOM_DOMAIN} per docs). If aud omits the issuer domain, failures are expected setup failures, not proof-integrity findings.

For I2 freshness tests on login_with_jwt, include a CONTROL login using a valid assertion alongside the ATTACK login. Without a control, LOGIN_FAILED on the attack assertion cannot be distinguished from broken key registration, wrong kid, wrong aud, or stale iat setup.

For I3 redirect_uri_mismatch tests on exchange_code_for_token, the redirect_uri in the token request MUST exactly match the redirect_uri used in start_oidc_auth. ZITADEL documents exact matching; mismatches are expected invalid_grant behavior, not identity confusion.

For I3 PKCE tests, ZITADEL supports only code_challenge_method=S256. Do not send plain or other methods when testing PKCE enforcement; unsupported methods cause expected flow failure unrelated to session binding.

For I3 PKCE-bound code exchange, if start_oidc_auth included code_challenge then exchange_code_for_token MUST send the matching code_verifier. Missing or wrong code_verifier is expected rejection and should be asserted via non-200/invalid_grant, not via identity comparison.

For OIDC login flows, state is only highly recommended, not documented as mandatory. Do not treat acceptance without state as a vulnerability by itself; use state only for client-side CSRF/session correlation in the fuzzer.

For OIDC login flows using implicit response types, nonce MUST be provided. ZITADEL documents nonce as mandatory for implicit flow; missing nonce causes expected request rejection and is not evidence of replay weakness.

For OIDC code-flow tests, nonce is recommended and should be sent by the fuzzer even though not documented as mandatory for code flow. This is necessary to test proper ID token replay/session binding semantics and avoid false positives from client-side omissions.

For I5 token-exchange audience tests, audience in token_exchange MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject_token and actor_token. Requests outside that subset are expected to fail by design; do not flag such failures as authorization bugs.

For I5 token-exchange scope-escalation tests, invalid_scope may be returned when requested scope exceeds the scope granted by the resource owner. Treat rejection as correct behavior; only flag success if the exchanged token actually carries broader scope/claims than upstream authorization permits.

For I5 token-exchange type tests, respect ZITADEL's supported token-type matrix: subject_token_type refresh_token is not allowed; requested_token_type defaults to access token if omitted; requested_token_type jwt is only valid for subject_token_type=jwt with actor_token; user_id subject tokens require actor_token. Unsupported combinations are expected setup failures.

For I5 token-exchange wrong-audience tests, introspection active=true is only returned when the requesting client is part of the token audience. If introspect_token returns active=false for a token outside the caller's audience, that is expected by design and should not be flagged as a bug.

For introspect_token and token/revoke, client authentication is required by an authorization method or headers. The fuzzer MUST supply either client_secret authentication or private_key_jwt/client_assertion as documented; 401 invalid_client without client auth is expected setup failure.

For exchange_code_for_token using client_secret_basic, OAuth requires form-url-encoding of client_id and client_secret before constructing the Basic header. Incorrect Basic encoding causes invalid_client and must not be misclassified as a security finding.

For exchange_code_for_token and token_exchange, session_token MUST map to access_token, not id_token. ZITADEL userinfo requires the access token of the user as Bearer token; using id_token for verify_granted_identity will fail for the wrong reason.

For I5 scope/claim tests using verify_granted_identity, claims returned by /oidc/v1/userinfo depend on granted scopes. Missing email/profile/roles/metadata claims without requesting the corresponding scopes is expected behavior, not under-issuance or over-issuance evidence.

For I5 audience tests, ZITADEL's access-token aud by default includes all client IDs and the project ID, and additional audiences can be requested via reserved scopes such as urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:{projectid}:aud. The fuzzer MUST account for these documented defaults/additions before concluding audience overbreadth.

For I5 organization-binding tests, requesting reserved scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} enforces that the user is a member of the selected organization; requesting urn:zitadel:iam:org:domain:primary:{domainname} enforces both organization membership and username suffix by that domain. Failures under these scopes are expected policy enforcement, not login bugs.

For I5 metadata claim tests, the reserved scope urn:zitadel:iam:user:metadata returns metadata values base64-encoded. The fuzzer MUST decode before semantic comparison; raw base64 strings are not evidence of type confusion or claim corruption.

For I1/JWKS rotation tests against ZITADEL as issuer, keys at /oauth/v2/keys are automatically rotated and clients are recommended to cache them. Acceptance of an old signing key during a cache window is standard JWKS caching behavior; only acceptance after cache refresh/expiry should be considered suspicious.

For I2 freshness tests on login_with_jwt, the JWT bearer grant documentation explicitly requires exp and iat in the assertion, with iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour and aud MUST include ZITADEL's issuing domain. Use a CONTROL assertion with exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} and iat={{now_epoch}} before concluding an attack token failed for security reasons.

For I1 JWT bearer tests against /oauth/v2/token, the assertion aud claim must include the ZITADEL issuing domain (https://${CUSTOM_DOMAIN} in docs). If aud does not target ZITADEL, rejection is expected and is not evidence of stronger issuer/key validation.
For I1 JWT bearer tests, the JWT header must carry a kid identifying the registered key. A missing or wrong kid can cause rejection before signature-trust logic under test is reached.

For I2 replay_same_token on oidc_jwt, do NOT flag successful reuse of the same valid JWT bearer access token across API calls as a vulnerability. ZITADEL documents bearer access tokens and standard OAuth/OIDC behavior; replay resistance is not implied for ordinary bearer tokens.

For I2 future_token tests, ZITADEL documents nbf as a claim available in JWT access tokens and introspection responses, but the provided docs do not explicitly state that nbf is enforced during JWT bearer grant validation. Acceptance of future-nbf tokens SHOULD be treated as potentially spec-compliant unless a control demonstrates explicit enforcement.
For I3 PKCE tests, ZITADEL supports only code_challenge_method=S256. Using plain or other methods will fail for configuration reasons, not because PKCE binding is correctly or incorrectly enforced.

For I3 PKCE skip tests, include client_id and code_verifier on the token request when testing the PKCE path. Omitting client_id in the PKCE exchange changes the request shape and can produce invalid_client/invalid_grant for the wrong reason.

For I3 state-swap style tests, state is only returned to the redirect_uri and is documented as CSRF mitigation, but the token endpoint itself binds on code plus exact redirect_uri. Do not treat token-endpoint behavior as state validation; state must be checked at the client/redirect handling layer.

For I5 scope-escalation tests on token_exchange and refresh flows, ZITADEL documents that requested scope may differ from the provided scope and that refresh-token scope must be a subset of the original authorization. Therefore, compare the returned scope and claims, not just request acceptance, when determining whether escalation occurred.

For I5 token_exchange_wrong_audience and token_exchange_ignore_audience tests, ZITADEL documents audience on token exchange as optional and requiring a subset of the combined audiences from subject and actor tokens. Tests MUST request an audience outside that allowed subset to probe enforcement; requesting an allowed subset is a valid success case.

For I5 token exchange token-type tests, subject_token_type semantics are strict. Only the documented identifiers are allowed, and some are disallowed or require actor_token. In particular, refresh_token is not allowed, jwt as subject_token is only allowed in combination with actor_token, and user_id is only allowed with actor_token. Rejections under these combinations are by design, not authorization-binding failures.

For I5 audience/claims verification, UserInfo returns claims depending on granted scopes, while introspection returns active plus token metadata and additional user claims depending on scopes. Missing profile/email claims without corresponding scopes is expected; do not treat absent claims as identity confusion or privilege stripping bugs.

For I5 reserved-scope tests, ZITADEL-specific scopes actively change authorization semantics. In particular, urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} enforces organization membership, urn:zitadel:iam:org:domain:primary:{domainname} enforces membership plus username suffix, and project:id:{projectid}:aud adds that project to the access-token audience. Tests must account for these scope side effects when interpreting success or failure.

For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, request expanded scopes and then verify whether returned scope and downstream claims exceed the original authorization. Because docs state returned scopes might differ from requested scopes, a successful HTTP response alone is insufficient evidence of escalation.

For introspect_token, client authentication is required by the documentation ('upon successful authorization of the client'). A 401 invalid_client without client auth is expected and must not be interpreted as token invalidity.

For I2 freshness tests on login_with_jwt, the JWT bearer assertion MUST include exp in the future and iat no older than 1 hour for the control case. Use exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} and iat={{now_epoch}}. ZITADEL documents that iat MUST NOT be older than 1h and exp is required in JWT profile examples; otherwise LOGIN_FAILED may reflect malformed assertion setup rather than the freshness attack under test.

For JWT bearer grant and private_key_jwt client authentication, the JWT aud claim MUST include ZITADEL's issuing domain (https://{domain}). Do NOT use token endpoint path as aud. Otherwise failures in I1/I5 tests may be caused by incorrect client assertion / grant construction rather than signature or claim validation behavior.

For JWT bearer grant and private_key_jwt client authentication, the JWT header MUST contain kid matching the downloaded keyId. ZITADEL documentation states kid is necessary to identify the key. Missing or wrong kid causes lookup failure unrelated to the invariant being tested.

For I2 expired_token tests on login_with_jwt, include a control assertion with exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} and iat={{now_epoch}} alongside the attack assertion. Without a control, rejection may be due to wrong aud, missing kid, or stale iat rather than expiry enforcement.

For I2 future_token tests on login_with_jwt, include a control assertion with exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} and iat={{now_epoch}} alongside the attack assertion. ZITADEL documents nbf as a claim surfaced in introspection/access tokens, but the provided docs do not explicitly state enforcement for incoming JWT bearer assertions; acceptance of future nbf MUST NOT be treated as a vulnerability without a control and separate confirmation.

For I5 token_exchange_wrong_audience and token_exchange_ignore_audience tests, requested audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from both subject_token and actor_token. If the requested audience is outside that subset, rejection is by design and not evidence of a broker-side authorization bug.

For token_exchange token type tests, respect ZITADEL's supported token-type matrix: subject_token_type=refresh_token is not allowed; requested_token_type=refresh_token is not allowed; subject_token_type=jwt is allowed only with actor_token; subject_token_type=user_id is allowed only with actor_token. Using unsupported combinations yields by-design failures and invalid test conclusions.

For I5 scope-escalation tests using token_exchange, invalid_scope responses are by design when requested scope exceeds the scope granted by the resource owner. The oracle MUST distinguish rejection from silent over-grant: only flag a violation if exchange succeeds and returns broader scope/claims than upstream authorization intent.

For OIDC authorization-code flow coherence tests (I3 state_swap/code_injection), redirect_uri at /oauth/v2/token MUST exactly match the redirect_uri used at /oauth/v2/authorize. ZITADEL documents exact matching; mismatches produce invalid_grant by design and must not be interpreted as session-binding success or failure.

For OIDC authorization requests, openid scope is mandatory. Any test omitting openid will trigger invalid_scope by design, which must not be interpreted as a security rejection related to audience, issuer, nonce, or state handling.

For OIDC implicit-flow tests, nonce MUST be provided. ZITADEL documents nonce as MUST for implicit flow. Missing nonce causes by-design request invalidation and cannot be used to infer replay protection behavior.

For OIDC code-flow tests, ZITADEL recommends state and nonce; state is highly recommended for CSRF mitigation and nonce binds client session to the ID token. To test I3 flow coherence correctly, the fuzzer SHOULD always send both state and nonce so failures are attributable to the intended mutation rather than missing baseline protections.

For PKCE-based code exchange, code_challenge_method must be S256; ZITADEL documents this as the only supported algorithm. Tests using plain or other methods will fail by design and should not be treated as proof of stronger validation semantics.

For verify_granted_identity on /oidc/v1/userinfo, the bearer token MUST be a user access_token, not a client_credentials token. ZITADEL explicitly states userinfo requires the access token of the user, not the client. Using machine tokens will produce misleading failures in identity-binding tests.

For introspect_token and revoke_session, client authentication is required by authorization method. The docs state these endpoints depend on additional parameters or headers and return invalid_client/401 on auth failure. The fuzzer MUST supply either client_secret authentication or private_key_jwt client assertion; otherwise failures are setup errors, not token-state findings.

For I1 alg_none/resign_attacker_key/kid-substitution tests against login_with_jwt, keep all non-signature fields valid simultaneously: aud includes issuer domain, iss/sub match key owner, exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}}, iat={{now_epoch}}, and kid matches the intended key identifier. Otherwise rejection may be caused by malformed grant construction instead of proof validation.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: Zitadel management API uses REST gateway paths under /management/v1/ (org-scoped). Do NOT use gRPC Connect paths. For IdP setup: create_provider creates the IdP, enable_auth_method adds it to the login policy with ownerType='IDP_OWNER_TYPE_ORG' (NOT 'ORG' or 'OWNER_TYPE_ORG'). Both are needed before IdP login works. SAML login is brokered — saml_login is NOT directly callable as a standalone POST. It is handled internally by the executor's ZITADEL-LOGIN flow triggered via start_oidc_auth with scope containing urn:zitadel:iam:org:idp:id:{idp_id}.
